title: Write maintainable technical documentation
description: Document setup, architecture, commands, data contracts and common troubleshooting paths from inspected evidence.
accomplishes: Document setup, architecture, commands, data contracts and common troubleshooting paths from inspected evidence. Explain ownership and safe change procedures. Separate verified commands from suggestions and note missing configuration. Avoid recording secrets or claiming undocumented behaviour is guaranteed.
prompt:
Act as a senior software engineer.

Task: Write maintainable technical documentation.

Input context:
- REPOSITORY: [REPOSITORY]
- MAINTAINERS: [MAINTAINERS]
- WORKFLOWS: [WORKFLOWS]
- KNOWN LIMITS: [KNOWN LIMITS]

Document setup, architecture, commands, data contracts and common troubleshooting paths from inspected evidence. Explain ownership and safe change procedures. Separate verified commands from suggestions and note missing configuration. Avoid recording secrets or claiming undocumented behaviour is guaranteed.

Preserve existing work and data. Define acceptance criteria and relevant checks. Separate plans, simulations and executed actions. No deployment without approval.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Maintainer documentation outline
Start with prerequisites and the exact local command, then describe source content, generated files and validation. Explain which build step owns each route and how to add an entry. Record deployment as a separate authorised workflow. Include known limitations and recovery steps so future maintainers do not edit generated output blindly.
